profile.summary: bacformer-causal-MAG is one released checkpoint of Bacformer, a model that treats a whole bacterial genome as a sequence of proteins ordered along the chromosome and plasmids. Each protein is embedded with the base protein language model ESM-2 t12 35M and the averaged embedding is used as one token, so the transformer returns, for every protein, a representation that depends on the other proteins in the same genome. This checkpoint was trained with an autoregressive objective, predicting the protein family of the next protein, on the MAG corpus of about 1.3 million metagenome-assembled genomes.
profile.summary_source_locator: Model card: opening section and Training Data; README opening paragraph

summary_quotes.text: Bacformer is a foundational model for bacterial genomics, modeling the whole bacterial genome as a sequence of proteins.

A key member of this collection is **bacformer-causal-MAG**, a 27M-parameter base transformer model trained on ~1.3M diverse metagenome-assembled genomes across more than 20k bacterial species and multiple environments.
Bacformer is a prokaryotic foundational model which models whole-bacterial genomes as a sequence of proteins ordered by their genomic coordinates on the chromosome and plasmid(s).

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each protein sequence of a genome is first embedded with a base protein language model and the amino acid token embeddings are averaged into one vector per protein. Those vectors are the tokens of a transformer of 12 layers and hidden size 480, which attends over all proteins of the genome and so returns contextual protein embeddings. Position is encoded with rotary positional embeddings and learnable contig embeddings mark which chromosome or plasmid each protein came from. The pretraining head does not predict amino acids: it predicts a discrete protein family index out of 50 thousand clusters, while the input stays the exact protein sequence.
sections.source_locator: Model card: Architecture, Input embeddings and Transformer backbone

quotes.text: Bacformer takes as input the set of proteins present in a genome, **ordered** by their positions on the chromosome and plasmid(s), and computes contextual protein representations with a transformer that conditions each protein on every other protein in the genome.
The transformer is 12 layer transformer with `hidden_dim=480` and is trained from scratch.
The genomic organisation is highly important for bacteria, to model it we employ **rotary positional embeddings**
The contig embeddings are learnable embeddings which represent the unique contigs present in the genome.
the classification head predicts the protein family. We predict protein family, rather than a protein, because the space of possible proteins is effectively unbound.

sections.title: What distinguishes this checkpoint
sections.body: The model card describes this checkpoint as a 27M-parameter transformer pretrained on about 1.3 million metagenome-assembled genomes covering more than 20 thousand bacterial species. Its objective is autoregressive: the protein family of the next protein is predicted from the preceding proteins. It takes protein embeddings from ESM-2 t12 35M.

quotes.text: A key member of this collection is **bacformer-causal-MAG**, a 27M-parameter base transformer model trained on ~1.3M diverse metagenome-assembled genomes across more than 20k bacterial species and multiple environments.
**bacformer-causal-MAG** was pretrained on the **MAG corpus** (≈1.3 M metagenome-assembled genomes).
The model was optimised to predict the next protein given previous proteins present in the genome.
Bacformer uses [ESM-2 t12 35 M](https://huggingface.co/facebook/esm2_t12_35M_UR50D) as its base model.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: A result should name the Hugging Face repository macwiatrak/bacformer-causal-MAG and the revision it used; this page was written from revision e4c8d6dc4decaa88729ce3853b1f329fee3b4960, which the Hugging Face API reported on 2026-11-27. The README table lists eight checkpoints. It describes bacformer-masked-MAG and bacformer-causal-MAG as 26M parameter models pretrained on about 1.3 million metagenome-assembled genomes, with a masked and an autoregressive objective; bacformer-masked-complete-genomes and bacformer-causal-complete-genomes as those two MAG models finetuned on about 40 thousand complete genomes; bacformer-large-masked-MAG and bacformer-large-masked-complete-genomes with the same text, a 300M parameter model pretrained on the MAG corpus with a masked objective; bacformer-causal-protein-family-modeling-complete-genomes as bacformer-causal-MAG finetuned on about 40 thousand complete genomes with protein-family tokens as input; and bacformer-for-essential-genes-prediction as bacformer-masked-complete-genomes finetuned on the essential-genes prediction task. The README news list dates the Hugging Face release of Bacformer to 2025-05-15.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: 12-layer transformer with hidden size 480 over averaged ESM-2 t12 35M protein embeddings, with rotary positional embeddings, learnable contig embeddings and a protein-family classification head.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: The protein sequences of one genome, ordered by their position on the chromosome and plasmids, each embedded with ESM-2 t12 35M and averaged over amino acid tokens; contig identifiers mark which contig each protein belongs to.

quotes.text: Bacformer takes as input the set of proteins present in a genome, **ordered** by their positions on the chromosome and plasmid(s), and computes contextual protein representations with a transformer that conditions each protein on every other protein in the genome.
The contig embeddings are learnable embeddings which represent the unique contigs present in the genome.

It takes as input average protein embeddings from protein language models and computes contextualised protein embeddings conditional on other proteins present in the genome. Bacformer is trained on a diverse dataset of ~1.3M bacterial genomes and ~3B proteins.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: One contextual embedding per protein (the last hidden state), which can be averaged into a single genome embedding, and protein-family predictions over 50 thousand protein-family clusters from the pretraining head.

run_guide.summary: Install the bacformer package and compute contextual protein embeddings with the bacformer-causal-MAG checkpoint.
prerequisites: Python 3.10, which the README names as the version Bacformer was developed in.
PyTorch 2.2 or above and flash attention, as the README install section asks for.
A CUDA GPU: the usage examples in the sources set device to cuda:0.
Network access to Hugging Face, to download the bacformer-causal-MAG weights and the ESM-2 t12 35M base model.

steps.title: Load the checkpoint and embed a few proteins
steps.shell:
python3 - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel
from bacformer.pp import protein_seqs_to_bacformer_inputs

device = "cuda:0"
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("macwiatrak/bacformer-causal-MAG", trust_remote_code=True).to(device).eval().to(torch.bfloat16)

protein_sequences = [
    "MGYDLVAGFQKNVRTI",
    "MKAILVVLLG",
    "MQLIESRFYKDPWGNVHATC",
    "MSTNPKPQRFAWL",
]
inputs = protein_seqs_to_bacformer_inputs(
    protein_sequences,
    device=device,
    batch_size=128,
    max_n_proteins=6000,
)

with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs, return_dict=True)
print(outputs.keys())
PY
